kaigo-excretion-01-summary.heading: Urination, bowel movements and listening to wishes
paragraphs: Explain the route urine takes and the sensations associated with urination and bowel movements.
Quietly check the person’s wishes and promptly contact the appropriate staff member.

kaigo-excretion-01-knowledge-0.heading: From urine production to leaving the body
paragraphs: The kidneys remove waste and other substances from the blood and produce urine. The ureters are tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to the bladder. Urine stored temporarily in the bladder leaves the body through the urethra. The ureters and urethra have different roles and locations.

The feeling of wanting to pass urine is the urge to urinate. The cerebrum, brainstem and spinal cord also help regulate urination. Producing urine, sensing the urge and reaching the toilet to urinate are different abilities.

The textbook gives approximate learning examples of a bladder capacity of 500 milliliters and an urge to urinate at around 200–300 milliliters. These do not mean everyone feels the urge at the same volume or can safely wait at that volume. The male urethra is longer than the female urethra, and the prostate surrounds the male urethra. These are also basic facts for understanding urination.

kaigo-excretion-01-knowledge-1.heading: From food to stool formation
paragraphs: Food passes from the mouth through the esophagus, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. Chewing and saliva make food easier to digest in the mouth. Digestion continues in the stomach through gastric juices and other processes. Nutrients and water are absorbed in the small intestine. Water absorption and stool formation also continue as the contents pass through the large intestine.

The large intestine includes the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon. Stool collects in the rectum and leaves through the anus. The feeling of wanting to pass stool is the urge to have a bowel movement. This urge may weaken over time, so do not repeatedly ask people to hold it solely for staff convenience.

The bladder stores urine, while stool collects in the rectum. A person saying they want to use the toilet does not establish which urge they feel. Check what is needed in a way they feel comfortable discussing.

kaigo-excretion-01-knowledge-2.heading: Excretion, dignity and personal agency
paragraphs: Excretion is a bodily function that maintains health. Urine and stool can provide clues about health, but using the toilet is also something people may want to keep private. Respect individual feelings of embarrassment. Do not blame the person or ask detailed questions in public.

Ask about the person’s habits and wishes. Support the parts they need help with while preserving what they can do. Needing help does not mean their choices about toileting or communication can be ignored. Contact the appropriate person promptly; do not delay actual toileting for practice.

kaigo-excretion-01-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Hasebe-san is seated in a stable place in their room and has not moved yet. Toilet assistance will be arranged with the person responsible according to the individual plan. Visitors are in the corridor, so Hasebe-san wants to speak quietly.

kaigo-depth-19.heading: Identify which toileting action is difficult
paragraphs: Sensing the urge, finding the toilet, moving, handling clothing and cleaning oneself are different abilities. Difficulty reaching the toilet in time because of mobility or cognitive problems does not mean urine production has also been lost.

Ask which actions are difficult and provide the necessary help, such as directions, preparing the route or handling clothing. Do not rush to take over what the person can do. Afterward, also check clothing, skin, posture and the return journey.

If only clothing fastenings are difficult, do not assume a diaper is the only option. Waiting, being watched and concerns about odors can also be burdensome. Avoid criticism, quietly listen to the person’s wishes and arrange support.
This lesson explains which actions need support and why. Actual assistance follows the individual assessment, agreed methods, equipment instructions and practical training.

kaigo-excretion-01-words.heading: Vocabulary and expression reference
paragraphs: This vocabulary list is a reference. You do not need to memorize or read everything aloud in one day. Choose words and expressions needed for today’s situation and check unfamiliar words when necessary.
看護師（かんごし） — Nurse: a professional providing nursing care and assisting medical treatment. Report confirmed facts and consult them about changes in condition.
排泄（はいせつ） — Excretion: removing substances the body no longer needs. It includes urine and stool and also relates to processes such as sweating.
尿（にょう） — Urine: liquid produced by the kidneys that passes through the ureters, bladder and urethra to leave the body.
便（べん） — Stool: material that passes through the large intestine and other parts after digestion and absorption and leaves through the anus.
尿意（にょうい） — Urge to urinate: the feeling of wanting to pass urine.
便意（べんい） — Urge to have a bowel movement: the feeling of wanting to pass stool.
羞恥心（しゅうちしん） — Embarrassment: feeling embarrassed about being seen or having something known. Ask the person how they feel.
失禁（しっきん） — Incontinence: urine or stool escaping involuntarily. It is not a reason to blame the person.
便座（べんざ） — Toilet seat: the sitting surface that supports the body when using a toilet.
尿器（にょうき） — Urinal: a device for collecting urine. Knowing about a device is different from being able to select and use it appropriately.
おむつ（おむつ） — Diaper: an item worn to collect urine or stool. Its use does not establish the person’s overall abilities.
腎臓（じんぞう） — Kidney: an organ that removes waste and other substances from the blood and produces urine.
膀胱（ぼうこう） — Bladder: a sac-like organ that temporarily stores urine.
尿道（にょうどう） — Urethra: the passage carrying urine from the bladder out of the body. It is different from a ureter.
大腸（だいちょう） — Large intestine: the intestine following the small intestine, involved in water absorption and stool formation.
上げる（あげる） — Raise: here, returning lowered clothing upward, as in pulling up pants.
足元（あしもと） — Feet and the area around them: check that clothing or equipment is not obstructing movement around the feet.
陰部（いんぶ） — Genital area: the external genitals and surrounding area. Respect privacy, check the necessary extent of care and minimize exposure.
浣腸（かんちょう） — Enema: a procedure introducing liquid or another substance through the anus to encourage a bowel movement. Learning this word does not authorize you to perform it yourself.
着替える（きがえる） — Change clothes: take off the clothing being worn and put on other clothing.
下げる（さげる） — Lower: here, moving clothing downward, as in lowering pants.
使い捨て手袋（つかいすててぶくろ） — Disposable gloves: gloves intended for one use. Remove them appropriately after dirty tasks and perform hand hygiene.
ポータブルトイレ（ぽーたぶるといれ） — Portable toilet: a movable toilet used in places such as a person’s room. Use it in a way appropriate to their condition and plan.
職員（しょくいん） — Staff member: a person working in the facility or organization. Distinguish people’s responsibilities when contacting them.
パジャマ（ぱじゃま） — Pajamas: clothing worn for sleep and similar occasions.
呼び出しボタン（よびだしぼたん） — Call button: a button signaling that a staff member is needed. Check that it works, is within reach and the person understands and can use it.
Useful expression: I’ll speak quietly with you here. What would you like regarding using the toilet?
Useful expression: I’ll tell only the staff who need to know, somewhere others cannot hear. I won’t discuss it loudly in the corridor.

kaigo-excretion-01-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] Hasebe-san is seated in a stable place in their room and has not moved yet. Toilet assistance will be arranged with the person responsible according to the individual plan. Visitors are in the corridor, so Hasebe-san wants to speak quietly.
Kenichi Hasebe: There are visitors in the corridor, so please keep your voice down. I want to talk about using the toilet.
Care worker: I’ll speak quietly with you here. What would you like regarding using the toilet?
Kenichi Hasebe: I need to urinate now. I’d like help getting to the toilet.
Care worker: You feel the urge to urinate now and need help getting to the toilet. I’ll arrange assistance with the person responsible according to the plan.
Kenichi Hasebe: Yes. I don’t want to discuss this where there are lots of people.
Care worker: I’ll tell only the staff who need to know, somewhere others cannot hear. I won’t discuss it loudly in the corridor.
Kenichi Hasebe: That’s reassuring. Could you call the person responsible?
Care worker: Yes. I’ll contact them right away and ask them to help.

kaigo-excretion-01-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A person quietly says they feel the urge to have a bowel movement and asks for help getting to the toilet. Their individual plan requires arranging assistance with the responsible staff member.
First, quietly confirm the urge to have a bowel movement and the help requested, then promptly tell the responsible staff member.
Do not report this as an urge to urinate or start a transfer you have not been trained to perform. Distinguish contacting someone from checking whether assistance was actually provided.

kaigo-excretion-01-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
Communication note
Hasebe-san: Currently feels the urge to urinate and wants help getting to the toilet.
Wish: Speak where others cannot hear.
Care worker: Contact the person responsible immediately according to the plan and arrange assistance. Movement has not started yet.

kaigo-language-transfer-221.heading: Read what the person wants to do first
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] Staff member: Would you like to return to your room first? Person: No, I’d like to use the toilet first. Staff member: I’ll check what assistance you need.
The person wants to use the toilet before returning to their room. The staff member is checking the assistance needed. The text does not say that movement or toileting assistance is complete.

kaigo-excretion-02-summary.heading: Toileting actions, privacy and safety
paragraphs: Understand toileting as a sequence of actions and distinguish what the person can do from the help needed.
Check the calling method and supervision plan to support both safety and privacy.

kaigo-excretion-02-knowledge-0.heading: One action does not establish overall independence
paragraphs: Toileting involves several actions: recognizing the urge, reaching the place, lowering clothing, adjusting posture, passing urine or stool, cleaning oneself, raising clothing and returning safely. Check each action to understand what the person can do independently.

Someone able to sit on a toilet seat may still need help adjusting clothing, wiping or returning. Conversely, difficulty handling clothing does not mean the ability to communicate an urge or choose a destination has been lost. One difficulty should not lead to taking over every action.

kaigo-excretion-02-knowledge-1.heading: A usable calling method and privacy
paragraphs: Check the route, floor, lighting, transfer space and grab bars. A grab bar must suit the person’s physical condition and the action involved; a nearby object is not necessarily suitable support. Also check entry, exit and transfer conditions when a wheelchair is used.

A call button signals difficulty or that the person has finished. Check that it works, is within reach and the person understands and can press it. Within the individual plan, balance screening the person from view with doors or curtains and maintaining necessary supervision.

kaigo-excretion-02-knowledge-2.heading: Clothing and posture for a person with hemiplegia
paragraphs: The textbook gives an example of a person with left-sided paralysis using a grab bar with the unaffected side while a staff member supports the affected side. It assumes that person’s abilities and conditions. Do not assume everyone can transfer while standing; check the individually agreed method.

Holding a grab bar to maintain posture and handling clothing are different tasks. Pulling clothing up as far as possible while sitting stably can reduce the work needed when standing. The person should complete the remaining part while standing only if that posture is stable.

Provide an explanation, obtain consent, arrange necessary screening, and prepare hand hygiene and protective equipment. Do not carry out transfers, seating or clothing assistance from written instructions alone; follow the procedures you have been trained in. Afterward, check clothing, posture, condition and the return route.

kaigo-excretion-02-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You are discussing later toileting assistance with Onodera-san in their room. They ask whether they can be alone in the toilet. The supervision method and staff waiting place are unconfirmed. Assistance has not started, and you have not promised to leave them waiting alone.

kaigo-depth-20.heading: Maintain necessary supervision while protecting privacy
paragraphs: Check the toilet entrance, floor, transfer space, grab bars the person can use and the call button. Closing the door does not automatically make the situation safe. Even if a button exists, the person may be unable to reach or use it.

Before starting, prepare necessary supplies and protective equipment and check the person’s wishes, calling method and which parts need assistance. Check posture during standing, sitting and clothing handling. When moving from dirty work to handling clean items, change gloves and perform hand hygiene appropriately.

The textbook includes an example in which the worker steps outside, but this does not apply to everyone. If sitting is unstable or the person cannot use the button, maintain the necessary proximity and supervision according to the individual plan. Listen to their wishes and explain how safety can be maintained.

After use, complete necessary personal cleaning, equipment and environmental handling, and hand hygiene. Communicate the confirmed waiting place and calling method. Do not promise the person will be fine alone while these remain unconfirmed.

kaigo-depth-21.heading: Separate clothing handling from body support
paragraphs: If someone can stand because they hold a grab bar with the unaffected hand, immediately asking them to pull up their pants with both hands removes needed support. Distinguish standing with support from standing without it.

In the hemiplegia example, the worker provides necessary support from the affected side and assists clothing handling and sitting as separate actions. Decide how to preserve privacy after seated stability is established. Afterward, adjusting clothing as far as possible while seated reduces the work needed in standing.

A stable posture is also required when standing to finish adjusting clothing. Do not support the body by pulling the affected arm or move with clothing tangled around the feet. Check grab-bar location and how the person uses it.

Provide transfers and standing support within the person’s authorized method and your training. Do not directly apply the textbook’s left-sided paralysis example to people with different paralysis or transfer methods.

To explain a posture that may ease bowel movements, the textbook gives an example of leaning forward and raising the heels. It helps learners consider the route from rectum to anus. It does not mean asking everyone to adopt this posture without checking stability, pain and other conditions. Check foot and body support individually.

kaigo-excretion-02-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You are discussing later toileting assistance with Onodera-san in their room. They ask whether they can be alone in the toilet. The supervision method and staff waiting place are unconfirmed. Assistance has not started, and you have not promised to leave them waiting alone.
Fumi Onodera: I’d like to be alone in the toilet, but can I call if I need help?
Care worker: You’d like to be alone and want to check whether you can call when you need help. I’ll check the supervision plan with the person responsible.
Fumi Onodera: Is having a button enough?
Care worker: A button alone is not enough. I’ll check whether you can reach and use it and what supervision is needed.
Fumi Onodera: Will you be waiting outside?
Care worker: The waiting place has not been decided yet. After checking the plan, I’ll explain where it is and how to call.
Fumi Onodera: Please explain it before we start, once it’s decided.
Care worker: Before starting, I’ll explain the confirmed supervision and calling methods and ask about your wishes again.

kaigo-excretion-02-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The person wants to be alone while using the toilet. The staff supervision method and waiting place have not yet been confirmed.
Acknowledge the wish, check how the person can call and what supervision is needed with the person responsible, then explain.
Do not assume a button is safe for everyone simply because it exists. Do not promise to wait outside before checking.

kaigo-excretion-02-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
Advance discussion record
Onodera-san: Wants to be alone and to know how to call if help is needed.
Supervision method and staff waiting place: Unconfirmed.
Check with the person responsible and explain to the person before starting.

kaigo-language-transfer-223.heading: Distinguish the button’s purpose from usable operation
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] Person: What is this button? Staff member: It’s a button to call staff. May I check whether you can press it?
The button is for calling staff. Explaining its name alone does not confirm that it works or the person can reach and press it. With the person’s consent, check how usable it actually is.

kaigo-excretion-03-summary.heading: Observe and report changes in stool and urine
paragraphs: Distinguish the person’s reported concerns, actual observations and unconfirmed records.
Report differences from the usual condition and the time. Do not independently diagnose or suggest medication.

kaigo-excretion-03-knowledge-0.heading: Compare urine and stool with the usual pattern
paragraphs: For urine, check matters such as amount, frequency, color and odor. For stool, check frequency, amount, color and form. Record the time and the person’s usual pattern too. Food, illness and environment can influence these, so do not determine a disease from one color or frequency alone.

The textbook gives urine examples of 1,000–1,500 milliliters and four to six times a day. Its examples describe a large amount as 2,000–3,000 milliliters or more and a small amount as 300–500 milliliters or less. It also gives frequent-urination examples of eight or more daytime episodes and two or more nighttime episodes. These are textbook reference examples, not criteria for a care worker to diagnose independently.

Describe and report cloudy urine, dark brown or red urine, strong odor and other observations specifically. The textbook’s description of pale yellow to clear urine alone cannot establish individual safety. Distinguish no entry in the record from having observed no change.

kaigo-excretion-03-knowledge-1.heading: Constipation, diarrhea and individual differences
paragraphs: For constipation, check not only reduced frequency or amount compared with usual, but also hard stool, difficulty passing it and a feeling of incomplete emptying. Functional constipation related to bodily function differs in possible mechanism from organic constipation, where a tumor, inflammation or another structural issue obstructs the passage. Do not establish the type from the person’s statement alone.

Diarrhea means passing loose, watery stool. Be aware of fluid loss and the risk of irritation damaging skin around the anus. Sudden diarrhea may raise concern about infection, so report it to a healthcare professional.

Regular toileting habits, fluids, dietary fiber and physical activity are factors to consider in constipation support. However, check conditions in the person’s situation and plan; do not recommend the same fluid intake or exercise to everyone. Tell a healthcare professional about persistent constipation or changes in condition.

For people with diarrhea who can drink orally, the textbook gives examples of plain warm water and room-temperature sports drinks. However, check that the person can drink and whether individual fluid or dietary conditions apply. Do not treat a drink name as a universal instruction. Follow healthcare guidance and the plan when supporting prevention of dehydration.

kaigo-excretion-03-knowledge-2.heading: Separate reported concerns, observations and unknowns
paragraphs: If the person says they have not had a bowel movement today, record their statement and when you heard it. You cannot claim to have observed hours when you were not on duty. If the night-shift record or usual bowel pattern is unconfirmed, report it as unconfirmed.

When there is a change, distinguish confirmed conditions from unconfirmed matters in your report to the nurse. If urgency is high, do not wait for every record to be collected. Reading this material alone does not authorize decisions or actions involving medication, enemas or changes in fluid intake.

kaigo-excretion-03-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 9:10, Morikawa-san says, ‘I haven’t had a bowel movement yet today, and I’m worried.’ Your shift started at 9:00. You have not checked the night-shift record or usual bowel pattern. No emergency is described, but you first report the concern to nurse Fujino-san and proceed with checking.

kaigo-depth-18.heading: Record stool color, form and changes specifically
paragraphs: Describe stool form by what you observe: hard small lumps, formed stool, soft stool or watery stool. The textbook describes brown stool and one or two bowel movements daily as usual examples, but comparison with the person’s normal pattern is necessary.

Describe changes such as red, black or whitish stool specifically. Food and illness can affect color. Do not conclude that black stool alone establishes bleeding or decide there is no problem while the cause remains unknown.

Record date and time, confirmed amounts and frequency, form and color, and the person’s words about pain or other symptoms separately. Show unconfirmed symptoms and information as unconfirmed and report changes to a healthcare professional. Also watch for dehydration and skin irritation with sudden diarrhea.

Do not independently recommend laxatives or antidiarrheal medication. Consider not just low frequency but differences from usual, the person’s difficulties and overall condition, and arrange the necessary assessment.

Aya Fujino: What would you like to report about Morikawa-san?
Care worker: At 9:10, Morikawa-san said, ‘I haven’t had a bowel movement yet today, and I’m worried.’ I’ve been on duty since 9:00.
Aya Fujino: Have you checked the night-shift record or usual bowel pattern?
Care worker: Not yet. I haven’t observed the whole day, so I’m distinguishing the person’s words from unconfirmed information in my report.
Aya Fujino: Thank you for letting me know first. Please tell me the results after checking the records.
Care worker: I’ll check the records and report what I find and what I cannot confirm to Fujino-san. I won’t independently decide this is constipation or recommend medication.
Aya Fujino: Yes. Please also record that the person is worried.
Care worker: I’ll record their concern and exact words with the time, then report the checking results to you.

kaigo-excretion-03-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A person tells a worker whose shift began at 7:00, ‘I passed urine many times last night.’ The worker has not read the night-shift record yet.
Distinguish when you heard the statement, the person’s words and the period you could observe. Check the record according to assigned responsibilities and report the results.
Do not invent a frequency or establish a disease. Leave unconfirmed information clearly marked as unconfirmed.

kaigo-excretion-03-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
9:10 report
Morikawa-san’s words: ‘I haven’t had a bowel movement yet today, and I’m worried.’
Reporter’s shift started: 9:00.
Night-shift record and usual bowel pattern: Unconfirmed.
Reported to Fujino. Report again after checking the record.

kaigo-language-transfer-247.heading: Distinguish daytime and nighttime equipment and support
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] During the day, the person uses the toilet. At night, they use a portable toilet. Help with clothing is needed for both.
The plan is to use the toilet during the day and a portable toilet at night. Clothing assistance is needed at both times, so the device alone does not establish independence in the whole sequence.

kaigo-excretion-04-summary.heading: Distinguish equipment purposes and incontinence mechanisms
paragraphs: Explain the purposes of toileting equipment and the main mechanisms of urinary incontinence.
Check differences between prepared equipment and the current plan before use.

kaigo-excretion-04-knowledge-0.heading: Match toileting equipment to purpose and condition
paragraphs: A portable toilet may be used when the person feels the urge but has difficulty reaching the toilet, or at night. A urinal collects urine; a bedpan collects stool or other waste in bed. Requirements such as sitting stability and mobility differ.

Diapers and absorbent pads are options for situations such as incontinence. However, using a diaper does not mean the person lacks the urge to urinate, cannot use the toilet or need not be asked about their wishes. Check abilities and wishes and use a method consistent with the current plan.

kaigo-excretion-04-knowledge-1.heading: Different mechanisms of urinary incontinence
paragraphs: Urinary incontinence is involuntary urine leakage. Distinguish stress incontinence, where urine leaks under abdominal pressure from coughing or sneezing, from urge incontinence, where a sudden strong urge is difficult to hold and the person cannot reach the toilet in time.

Overflow incontinence may involve urine leaking gradually when difficulty emptying leaves urine in the bladder. Reflex incontinence occurs with impaired urination control, such as after spinal cord injury. The word ‘leaked’ alone does not establish the same mechanism. The material gives obstruction due to an enlarged prostate as one possible cause of overflow incontinence. Reflex examples include leakage without feeling an urge. These examples explain mechanisms; do not establish the cause from the person’s account or leakage pattern alone.

Functional urinary incontinence involves factors such as not managing movement or clothing in time, or not finding the toilet because of dementia. These categories support understanding. Care workers report actual circumstances and seek healthcare assessment of type and cause.

kaigo-excretion-04-knowledge-2.heading: Preparing urinals and bedpans and completing care
paragraphs: Prepare clean equipment, waterproof protection and necessary protective equipment, explain and obtain consent. Use curtains or towels to avoid unnecessary exposure and adjust posture and bed height to the person. The right equipment name does not guarantee a suitable shape or position.

For a bedpan, check alignment with the anus, body support, pain and stability. For a urinal, support a posture appropriate to the person and product to avoid leaks or splashes. Do not force someone unable to lift their hips to do so; choose a method you have been trained in.

After use, remove the equipment, provide necessary cleaning and skin observation, adjust clothing, return the bed to a safe height, check the person’s condition and tidy up. Removing the equipment alone does not complete the task.

kaigo-excretion-04-knowledge-3.heading: Do not replace actual facts with category labels
paragraphs: [Learning comparison] Leakage with coughing, a strong urge, gradual small leaks and a blocked route to the toilet are different pieces of information. Record the observation time and the person’s words. Do not record an incontinence category as a diagnosis based on a single event.

Preparing equipment is also different from deciding to change the method. If prepared items conflict with the plan, tell the appropriate person responsible both facts and check the current plan. Record only wishes actually confirmed with the person.

kaigo-excretion-04-knowledge-4.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In the staff room, you confirm Hasebe-san’s record specifies assistance in the toilet. However, a colleague says a portable toilet has been prepared in the room. Whether the current plan has changed is unconfirmed. The equipment has not been used yet.

kaigo-depth-22.heading: Urinal and bedpan position and body support
paragraphs: A bedpan must be aligned to receive waste from the anus while the body remains stable. Match the urinal’s shape and the person’s posture and check its position to collect urine. Gender alone does not determine movement or the assistance needed.

Prepare an explanation and consent, screening, waterproof protection, clean equipment and protective equipment, then set the bed to a suitable working height. Let people who can lift their hips do what they can, but do not force those who cannot. Choose the support method you have been trained in.

Do not forcefully drag equipment under the skin. Check position, stability, pain and discomfort. When using a urinal, arrange necessary body support and consider leaks and splashes. Before changing posture, such as raising the back, check the method allowed for the person.

After use, complete removal, personal cleaning, skin observation, clothing and bedding adjustment, restoring the bed, checking the person’s condition and tidying up. Covering the person with a towel alone does not establish comfort.

kaigo-excretion-04-words.heading: Vocabulary and expression reference
paragraphs: This vocabulary list is a reference. You do not need to memorize or read everything aloud in one day. Choose words and expressions needed for today’s situation and check unfamiliar words when necessary.
看護師（かんごし） — Nurse: a professional providing nursing care and assisting medical treatment. Report confirmed facts and consult them about changes in condition.
排泄（はいせつ） — Excretion: removing substances the body no longer needs. It includes urine and stool and also relates to processes such as sweating.
尿（にょう） — Urine: liquid produced by the kidneys that passes through the ureters, bladder and urethra to leave the body.
便（べん） — Stool: material that passes through the large intestine and other parts after digestion and absorption and leaves through the anus.
尿意（にょうい） — Urge to urinate: the feeling of wanting to pass urine.
便意（べんい） — Urge to have a bowel movement: the feeling of wanting to pass stool.
羞恥心（しゅうちしん） — Embarrassment: feeling embarrassed about being seen or having something known. Ask the person how they feel.
失禁（しっきん） — Incontinence: urine or stool escaping involuntarily. It is not a reason to blame the person.
便座（べんざ） — Toilet seat: the sitting surface that supports the body when using a toilet.
尿器（にょうき） — Urinal: a device for collecting urine. Knowing about a device is different from being able to select and use it appropriately.
ポータブルトイレ（ポータブルトイレ） — Portable toilet: a movable toilet used in places such as a person’s room. Use it in a way appropriate to their condition and plan.
おむつ（おむつ） — Diaper: an item worn to collect urine or stool. Its use does not establish the person’s overall abilities.
上げる（あげる） — Raise: here, returning lowered clothing upward, as in pulling up pants.
足元（あしもと） — Feet and the area around them: check that clothing or equipment is not obstructing movement around the feet.
陰部（いんぶ） — Genital area: the external genitals and surrounding area. Respect privacy, check the necessary extent of care and minimize exposure.
浣腸（かんちょう） — Enema: a procedure introducing liquid or another substance through the anus to encourage a bowel movement. Learning this word does not authorize you to perform it yourself.
着替える（きがえる） — Change clothes: take off the clothing being worn and put on other clothing.
下げる（さげる） — Lower: here, moving clothing downward, as in lowering pants.
使い捨て手袋（つかいすててぶくろ） — Disposable gloves: gloves intended for one use. Remove them appropriately after dirty tasks and perform hand hygiene.
職員（しょくいん） — Staff member: a person working in the facility or organization. Distinguish people’s responsibilities when contacting them.
パジャマ（ぱじゃま） — Pajamas: clothing worn for sleep and similar occasions.
呼び出しボタン（よびだしぼたん） — Call button: a button signaling that a staff member is needed. Check that it works, is within reach and the person understands and can use it.
Useful expression: The individual record says to assist in the toilet, but a colleague told me a portable toilet has been prepared in the room. I’d like to check whether there has been a change.
Useful expression: Kawase-san will check the current plan, and I’ll tell the colleague the result. I won’t change the equipment myself before checking.

kaigo-excretion-04-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In the staff room, you confirm Hasebe-san’s record specifies assistance in the toilet. However, a colleague says a portable toilet has been prepared in the room. Whether the current plan has changed is unconfirmed. The equipment has not been used yet.
Naoto Kawase: Is there something you want to check about Hasebe-san’s support?
Care worker: The individual record says to assist in the toilet, but a colleague told me a portable toilet has been prepared in the room. I’d like to check whether there has been a change.
Naoto Kawase: Prepared equipment alone does not establish a change in the plan. Have you used it yet?
Care worker: No, not yet. I haven’t treated its preparation as a new instruction.
Naoto Kawase: I’ll check the current plan. Please tell the colleague what is confirmed.
Care worker: Kawase-san will check the current plan, and I’ll tell the colleague the result. I won’t change the equipment myself before checking.
Naoto Kawase: Yes. Record only the wishes actually confirmed with the person, too.
Care worker: I’ll record the equipment–plan difference, checking results and confirmed wishes separately.

kaigo-excretion-04-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A diaper has been prepared, but the individual record specifies help getting to the toilet. Why the diaper was placed there is unconfirmed.
Tell the person responsible about both the record and prepared item, then check the current plan and the person’s wishes.
Do not assume that the person cannot use the toilet merely because a diaper is present, or change the method yourself.

kaigo-excretion-04-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
Request for checking
Hasebe-san’s record: Support in the toilet according to the plan.
Information from colleague: A portable toilet has been prepared in the room. Not used yet.
Kawase: Check the current plan. Reporter: Tell the colleague the result.

kaigo-language-transfer-222.heading: Distinguish planned preparation from completed preparation
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] Colleague: We plan to prepare a portable toilet today. Staff member: I’ll check the current plan before preparing it.
This describes a plan to prepare equipment. The staff member says they will check the current plan first. Nothing says preparation or use is already complete.

kaigo-excretion-05-summary.heading: Consider diaper changing and genital cleanliness
paragraphs: Explain information and consent, and the distinction between clean and dirty work, during diaper changing.
Do not assume the cause of wetness. Check the wish to change clothes and who may be told.

kaigo-excretion-05-knowledge-0.heading: Check the person and preparations before changing
paragraphs: Before changing a diaper, check the person’s condition, explain the purpose and actions and obtain consent. Ask about wishes and actions they can do, prepare necessary supplies and separate places for clean and used items.

Follow the person’s condition and your trained method for turning and bed height. Prepare waterproof protection and expose only necessary areas. One episode of wetness does not justify deciding that all future care will use diapers.

kaigo-excretion-05-knowledge-1.heading: Genital cleaning and the transition from dirty to clean
paragraphs: When removing urine or stool, avoid spreading it to other areas. For female genital cleaning, learn the principle of washing or wiping from the urethral side toward the anus, front to back. Do not move a soiled surface back and forth. Gently clean overlapping skin areas too.

Genital skin is sensitive to temperature. The textbook gives water around body temperature as an example, but check the person’s sensation, skin and facility procedure; do not use excessively hot water. After washing, gently dry away remaining moisture.

Handle the used diaper with the contaminated surface folded inward. Do not handle clean diapers or clothes with gloves that touched waste. Change gloves and perform hand hygiene at task transitions. Do not assume the textbook illustrations show every infection-control step; follow the facility procedures you have been trained in.

kaigo-excretion-05-knowledge-2.heading: Check tightness, wrinkles and condition
paragraphs: Check the new diaper’s type and size and fit it to the body. Excessive tightness around the abdomen or thighs can cause discomfort and skin problems. Wrinkled clothing or sheets can also contribute to discomfort and pressure injuries.

For a taped diaper example, the textbook describes checking space for two or three fingers at the abdomen and thighs. This is not a measurement method for every product. Follow product instructions and the individual method, and actually check skin, the person’s comfort, clothing, bedding and posture.

Complete ventilation, tidying and another condition check. Report observed redness, pain, wounds or other changes without independently treating them. Learn diaper-changing techniques through practical training rather than performing them from text alone.

kaigo-excretion-05-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In their room, Hasebe-san says their pants are wet and they want to change. They do not want visitors to know. The cause of the wetness is unconfirmed. Listen to their wishes and arrange support from trained staff according to the plan.

kaigo-depth-23.heading: Separate dirty and clean work during diaper changes
paragraphs: A diaper is one toileting aid. It does not itself ensure clean skin or opportunities to use the toilet. Check the appropriate product, size and posture, and keep clean items away from contaminated surfaces.

Obtain consent, prepare screening and waterproof protection and change posture using your trained method. Fold the dirty diaper’s inner surface inward, gently wash necessary areas and dry them. Change gloves and perform hand hygiene when moving from dirty to clean items.

Smooth the new diaper’s wrinkles and rolled-in edges and avoid excessive tightness around the abdomen and thighs. Do not apply the textbook’s finger-count example to all products; adjust according to product instructions. Also arrange clothing and bedding.

Check not only for leaks, but also redness, moisture, wounds, pain and discomfort. Do not rush using untrained methods such as pulling the legs to turn the body. Report skin changes to a healthcare professional without treating them independently.

kaigo-excretion-05-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] In their room, Hasebe-san says their pants are wet and they want to change. They do not want visitors to know. The cause of the wetness is unconfirmed. Listen to their wishes and arrange support from trained staff according to the plan.
Kenichi Hasebe: My pants are wet. I don’t want the visitors to know.
Care worker: I’ll ask where others cannot hear. What help would you like now, such as changing clothes?
Kenichi Hasebe: I want to change. You can call the staff who need to help, but please don’t tell the visitors.
Care worker: I’ll quietly ask only the necessary staff for help changing. I won’t tell the visitors about this.
Kenichi Hasebe: What will you say if they ask why they’re wet?
Care worker: I’ll say the cause has not been confirmed. I won’t assume incontinence; I’ll report confirmed facts and your wishes separately.

kaigo-excretion-05-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] The person says, ‘My sheet is wet. I’d like it changed without others knowing.’ The cause is unconfirmed.
Quietly check the help requested and which staff may be contacted, then arrange necessary support.
Do not assume incontinence. Distinguish the person’s words from the unknown cause. If you have only arranged help, do not record the change as complete.

kaigo-excretion-05-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
Support request note
Hasebe-san’s words: ‘My pants are wet. I want to change.’
Cause: Unconfirmed.
Wishes: Necessary staff may be contacted. Do not tell visitors.
Arrange help changing. Completion has not yet been confirmed.

kaigo-language-transfer-220.heading: Distinguish observed redness from reported itching
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] Staff member: I found a red area on your right wrist. Person: It’s itchy there. Staff member: I’ll tell the nurse.
The worker saw redness on the right wrist; the person reported itching. They did not say it hurts. Tell the nurse the observation and reported symptom separately without assuming a cause.

kaigo-excretion-06-summary.heading: Read night-shift toileting records with their dates
paragraphs: Read the dates and times in records crossing midnight, and identify unconfirmed items accurately.
Distinguish subjective and objective facts and clarify responsibility for corrections and further checking.

kaigo-excretion-06-knowledge-0.heading: Do not confuse observations across midnight
paragraphs: Record both the date and time of toileting. The 11 p.m. hour on one day and the midnight hour the next are different dates. Do not copy a previous observation into the next day’s field or fill an unconfirmed amount with zero.

Color and odor are observations. ‘It was dark brown’ is an observed fact; ‘It is an infection’ is a judgment requiring assessment. Do not establish a cause from color or odor alone. Report confirmed facts to a healthcare professional.

kaigo-excretion-06-knowledge-1.heading: Types of facts and accurate recording
paragraphs: Make clear when, where, who, what and how in the record. Give reasons only where supported; do not fill unknown causes with speculation. Make the observed condition, staff action and the person’s response understandable.

Pain and anxiety reported by the person are subjective facts; conditions seen and values measured by staff are objective facts. Both are needed for support, but they are obtained differently. Record promptly using the facility’s method, and make corrections so the sequence remains traceable afterward.

kaigo-excretion-06-knowledge-2.heading: Clarify responsibilities and unknowns during handoff
paragraphs: The recipient repeats back necessary points and checks who will investigate further and who will receive the result. ‘Unconfirmed’ does not mean ‘no abnormality’ or ‘no urine or stool passed.’ When adding results later, distinguish when they were established.

Choose the reporting time and place to suit the information. Report changes needing urgent action immediately; do not delay a report to gather paperwork. Even at night, share personal information only with staff who need it and in a way others cannot hear.

kaigo-excretion-06-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You are reading Onodera-san’s record in a private handoff area. It records a bowel movement at 9:40 p.m. on October 6. The 6:30 a.m. entry on October 7 says the stool’s condition is unconfirmed. A colleague misunderstood this as an observation completed this morning, so you check the dates and entries.

kaigo-depth-37.heading: Check direction, cleanliness and the person’s feelings during genital cleaning
paragraphs: The genital and anal areas are readily exposed to urine, stool and moisture. Besides removing dirt, avoid damaging skin or transferring contamination elsewhere. For women, learn the principle of working from the urethral side toward the anus, front to back.

Explain the purpose, obtain consent and cover areas not currently being washed. Use necessary protective equipment, check water temperature and do not move a soiled surface back and forth over the same area. Gently clean necessary skin folds and dry away moisture. For men, do not overlook dirt beneath or around the scrotum; clean within your training. Do not pull with force or perform deeper manipulation.

Check redness, pain, wounds, moisture and other changes and report concerns. Before handling clean clothing or similar items, change gloves and perform hand hygiene at the transition from dirty work. If the person reports pain or wants to stop, listen and arrange necessary support.

External cleaning is different from procedures such as enemas or urinary catheterization. Knowing terminology does not authorize deeper manipulation or tube procedures. Follow the individual plan, facility procedures and practical training, and consult the person responsible about uncertain decisions.

kaigo-excretion-06-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] You are reading Onodera-san’s record in a private handoff area. It records a bowel movement at 9:40 p.m. on October 6. The 6:30 a.m. entry on October 7 says the stool’s condition is unconfirmed. A colleague misunderstood this as an observation completed this morning, so you check the dates and entries.
Misaki Kishimoto: So Onodera-san’s stool condition was checked at 6:30 this morning?
Care worker: The 6:30 entry says, ‘Stool condition unconfirmed.’ The bowel movement record is from 9:40 p.m. on October 6, a different date.
Misaki Kishimoto: Does that mean there was no bowel movement on the morning of October 7?
Care worker: This entry alone cannot establish that. It is the stool condition that is unconfirmed; this entry also does not establish whether there was a bowel movement this morning.
Misaki Kishimoto: I understand. I’ll correct the handoff explanation. Could you check the unconfirmed information?
Care worker: Kishimoto-san will correct the explanation, and I’ll check the unconfirmed information according to procedure. We’ll share the results afterward.
Misaki Kishimoto: Let’s also preserve the correction using the agreed method.
Care worker: I’ll record the correction using the agreed method, keep the original record rather than independently deleting it, and record the checking results separately.

kaigo-excretion-06-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] There is a urination record at 11:20 p.m. on October 8. The 6:00 a.m. field on October 9 says urine volume is unconfirmed.
Read the date and time together and identify which item is unconfirmed. Follow the assigned responsibilities and method for further checking.
Do not infer no urination or enter zero because the volume is missing. Do not turn the previous day’s result into the following day’s measurement.

kaigo-excretion-06-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
Onodera-san’s record
October 6, 9:40 p.m.: Bowel movement.
October 7, 6:30 a.m.: Stool condition unconfirmed. This field does not record whether there was a bowel movement this morning.
Correction: Kishimoto. Checking unconfirmed matters: Reporter.

kaigo-language-transfer-265.heading: Read the following day’s schedule with the date
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] Night-shift schedule: Prepare at 8:00 p.m. Check at 1:00 a.m. the following day and record at 7:00 a.m. Checking intervals follow the individual plan.

The schedule calls for checking at 1:00 a.m. the day after preparation and recording at 7:00 a.m. These times apply only to this learning schedule. They do not establish a rule to check everyone at the same intervals.

kaigo-excretion-07-summary.heading: Check wishes, arrangements and outcomes separately
paragraphs: Check the person’s wishes, communication results and actual implementation separately.
Promptly report to the person responsible so necessary assistance does not remain pending.

kaigo-excretion-07-knowledge-0.heading: From the person’s wishes to checking after support
paragraphs: Review the sequence of listening to wishes, checking the help needed for each action, supporting through agreed methods, maintaining cleanliness and safety, and checking the condition afterward. Someone able to do part independently does not necessarily need every action taken over.

Diaper use is separate from the person’s wishes and remaining abilities. Listen when they report an urge, want to use the toilet or need help only with clothing. Consider necessary assistance according to the current plan.

kaigo-excretion-07-knowledge-1.heading: The boundary between knowledge and practical skills
paragraphs: Urinals, bedpans, portable toilets and diapers differ in purpose and required posture. Knowing their names is not the same as being able to use them safely. Check the person’s condition, plan, product instructions and practical training.

Incontinence categories help identify differences in circumstances. They do not authorize independent decisions about equipment, diagnoses or medication changes. Consult the person responsible or a healthcare professional about unknown conditions, and do not record an action as complete before checking.

kaigo-excretion-07-knowledge-2.heading: Distinguish arrangements in progress from completed help
paragraphs: The person’s request, contacting staff, acceptance by the responsible person, providing assistance and the condition afterward are separate information. Hearing ‘I’ll arrange it’ does not establish that toileting assistance is complete.

Promptly check responsibility and implementation so currently needed support does not remain pending. Report unconfirmed matters as unconfirmed and contact the appropriate person. Tell necessary staff the person’s wishes while protecting their wish for privacy.

kaigo-excretion-07-knowledge-3.heading: Today’s practice situation
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 2:05 p.m., Morikawa-san requests toilet assistance and privacy from others hearing. A colleague says they will arrange it, but who accepted and whether anyone arrived are still unconfirmed. Without waiting until your shift ends, you tell Kawase-san in the staff room.

paragraphs: This vocabulary list is a reference. You do not need to memorize or read everything aloud in one day. Choose words and expressions needed for today’s situation and check unfamiliar words when necessary.
看護師（かんごし） — Nurse: a professional providing nursing care and assisting medical treatment. Report confirmed facts and consult them about changes in condition.
排泄（はいせつ） — Excretion: removing substances the body no longer needs. It includes urine and stool and also relates to processes such as sweating.
尿（にょう） — Urine: liquid produced by the kidneys that passes through the ureters, bladder and urethra to leave the body.
便（べん） — Stool: material that passes through the large intestine and other parts after digestion and absorption and leaves through the anus.
尿意（にょうい） — Urge to urinate: the feeling of wanting to pass urine.
便意（べんい） — Urge to have a bowel movement: the feeling of wanting to pass stool.
羞恥心（しゅうちしん） — Embarrassment: feeling embarrassed about being seen or having something known. Ask the person how they feel.
失禁（しっきん） — Incontinence: urine or stool escaping involuntarily. It is not a reason to blame the person.
便座（べんざ） — Toilet seat: the sitting surface that supports the body when using a toilet.
尿器（にょうき） — Urinal: a device for collecting urine. Knowing about a device is different from being able to select and use it appropriately.
ポータブルトイレ（ポータブルトイレ） — Portable toilet: a movable toilet used in places such as a person’s room. Use it in a way appropriate to their condition and plan.
おむつ（おむつ） — Diaper: an item worn to collect urine or stool. Its use does not establish the person’s overall abilities.
呼び出しボタン（よびだしボタン） — Call button: a button signaling that a staff member is needed. Check that it works, is within reach and the person understands and can use it.

便秘（べんぴ） — Constipation: difficulty passing enough stool comfortably, including hard stool, difficult or incomplete evacuation or less frequent bowel movements than usual. A blank entry alone does not establish it.
下痢（げり） — Diarrhea: passing loose, watery stool. Report changes without deciding the cause yourself.
上げる（あげる） — Raise: here, returning lowered clothing upward, as in pulling up pants.
足元（あしもと） — Feet and the area around them: check that clothing or equipment is not obstructing movement around the feet.
陰部（いんぶ） — Genital area: the external genitals and surrounding area. Respect privacy, check the necessary extent of care and minimize exposure.
浣腸（かんちょう） — Enema: a procedure introducing liquid or another substance through the anus to encourage a bowel movement. Learning this word does not authorize you to perform it yourself.
着替える（きがえる） — Change clothes: take off the clothing being worn and put on other clothing.
下げる（さげる） — Lower: here, moving clothing downward, as in lowering pants.
使い捨て手袋（つかいすててぶくろ） — Disposable gloves: gloves intended for one use. Remove them appropriately after dirty tasks and perform hand hygiene.
職員（しょくいん） — Staff member: a person working in the facility or organization. Distinguish people’s responsibilities when contacting them.
パジャマ（ぱじゃま） — Pajamas: clothing worn for sleep and similar occasions.

kaigo-excretion-07-dialogue.heading: Conversation in context
paragraphs: [Situation created for learning] At 2:05 p.m., Morikawa-san requests toilet assistance and privacy from others hearing. A colleague says they will arrange it, but who accepted and whether anyone arrived are still unconfirmed. Without waiting until your shift ends, you tell Kawase-san in the staff room.
Naoto Kawase: What have you confirmed so far about Morikawa-san’s wishes?
Care worker: At 2:05 p.m., Morikawa-san requested toilet assistance. They also said they do not want others to hear.
Naoto Kawase: Has it been decided who will help?
Care worker: A colleague said they would arrange it, but responsibility and implementation are unconfirmed. I can’t conclude it’s finished, so I’m telling you now.
Naoto Kawase: I’ll arrange a staff member to help. Please check the communication result and implementation.
Care worker: Kawase-san will arrange staff, and I’ll check the communication result and implementation. We’ll share quietly with only the staff who need to know.
Naoto Kawase: After checking, record the request, contact and implementation separately.
Care worker: I’ll separately record the request time, communication result and confirmed implementation. I’ll report anything I cannot confirm to Kawase-san as unconfirmed.

kaigo-excretion-07-transfer-legacy.heading: Apply your learning to another situation
paragraphs: [Another learning situation] A person wants to use the toilet immediately, and a colleague says they will arrange help. The responsible staff member and outcome are unconfirmed.
Tell the person responsible the request time and current known circumstances, then check who accepted the support and whether it was provided.
Do not consider the task complete merely because you contacted someone once. Share quietly with necessary staff and report unconfirmed matters as unconfirmed.

kaigo-excretion-07-reading.heading: Read records needed for support
paragraphs:
2:05 p.m. support request
Morikawa-san: Wants toilet assistance and privacy from others hearing.
Colleague’s reply: Said they would arrange it. Responsible staff and implementation: Unconfirmed.
Kawase: Arrange staff. Reporter: Check and report communication results and implementation.

kaigo-language-transfer-255.heading: Sitting ability does not establish safe waiting alone
paragraphs: [Text created for learning] The person can sit on a toilet seat. They need help with clothing. Whether they can use the call button has not been checked yet.
We know the person can sit and needs clothing assistance, but call-button use is unconfirmed. Do not promise to wait outside before checking the supervision plan and safety conditions.

kaigo-excretion-01.title: Urination, bowel movements and listening to wishes
objectives: Explain the route urine takes and the sensations associated with urination and bowel movements.
Quietly check the person’s wishes and promptly contact the appropriate staff member.
kaigo-excretion-01.context: [Situation created for learning] Hasebe-san is seated in a stable place in their room and has not moved yet. Toilet assistance will be arranged with the person responsible according to the individual plan. Visitors are in the corridor, so Hasebe-san wants to speak quietly.
kaigo-excretion-01.artCaption: Quietly listen to the person’s wishes and arrange toilet assistance with the person responsible.

kaigo-excretion-02.title: Toileting actions, privacy and safety
objectives: Understand toileting as a sequence of actions and distinguish what the person can do from the help needed.
Check the calling method and supervision plan to support both safety and privacy.
kaigo-excretion-02.context: [Situation created for learning] You are discussing later toileting assistance with Onodera-san in their room. They ask whether they can be alone in the toilet. The supervision method and staff waiting place are unconfirmed. Assistance has not started, and you have not promised to leave them waiting alone.
kaigo-excretion-02.artCaption: Listen to the wish to be alone and check calling methods and necessary supervision.

kaigo-excretion-03.title: Observe and report changes in stool and urine
objectives: Distinguish the person’s reported concerns, actual observations and unconfirmed records.
Report differences from the usual condition and the time. Do not independently diagnose or suggest medication.
kaigo-excretion-03.context: [Situation created for learning] At 9:10, Morikawa-san says, ‘I haven’t had a bowel movement yet today, and I’m worried.’ Your shift started at 9:00. You have not checked the night-shift record or usual bowel pattern. No emergency is described, but you first report the concern to nurse Fujino-san and proceed with checking.
kaigo-excretion-03.artCaption: Report the person’s words and confirmed records separately to the nurse.

kaigo-excretion-04.title: Distinguish equipment purposes and incontinence mechanisms
objectives: Explain the purposes of toileting equipment and the main mechanisms of urinary incontinence.
Check differences between prepared equipment and the current plan before use.
kaigo-excretion-04.context: [Situation created for learning] In the staff room, you confirm Hasebe-san’s record specifies assistance in the toilet. However, a colleague says a portable toilet has been prepared in the room. Whether the current plan has changed is unconfirmed. The equipment has not been used yet.
kaigo-excretion-04.artCaption: Communicate differences between records and prepared equipment and check the current plan.

kaigo-excretion-05.title: Consider diaper changing and genital cleanliness
objectives: Explain information and consent, and the distinction between clean and dirty work, during diaper changing.
Do not assume the cause of wetness. Check the wish to change clothes and who may be told.
kaigo-excretion-05.context: [Situation created for learning] In their room, Hasebe-san says their pants are wet and they want to change. They do not want visitors to know. The cause of the wetness is unconfirmed. Listen to their wishes and arrange support from trained staff according to the plan.
kaigo-excretion-05.artCaption: This scene shows preparation of clean supplies and protective equipment. It does not illustrate diaper-changing or genital-cleaning techniques.

kaigo-excretion-06.title: Read night-shift toileting records with their dates
objectives: Read the dates and times in records crossing midnight, and identify unconfirmed items accurately.
Distinguish subjective and objective facts and clarify responsibility for corrections and further checking.
kaigo-excretion-06.context: [Situation created for learning] You are reading Onodera-san’s record in a private handoff area. It records a bowel movement at 9:40 p.m. on October 6. The 6:30 a.m. entry on October 7 says the stool’s condition is unconfirmed. A colleague misunderstood this as an observation completed this morning, so you check the dates and entries.
kaigo-excretion-06.artCaption: Read the previous day’s record and the new field separately, checking dates, times and unconfirmed matters.

kaigo-excretion-07.title: Check wishes, arrangements and outcomes separately
objectives: Check the person’s wishes, communication results and actual implementation separately.
Promptly report to the person responsible so necessary assistance does not remain pending.
kaigo-excretion-07.context: [Situation created for learning] At 2:05 p.m., Morikawa-san requests toilet assistance and privacy from others hearing. A colleague says they will arrange it, but who accepted and whether anyone arrived are still unconfirmed. Without waiting until your shift ends, you tell Kawase-san in the staff room.
kaigo-excretion-07.artCaption: Report pending assistance to the person responsible and check who will provide it and whether it has been done.
